output.title: Observability pipeline
output.description: An invented platform team, Halyard Ops. Every request a shop service handles sends logs, spans and metrics to node agents, then through load-balanced gateway collectors that tail-sample traces, into Kafka. Kafka buffers each signal for its own backends, so an outage or a log storm in one never stalls the rest.

simulations.title: An incident log storm
simulations.description: A bad Checkout deploy logs every retry: telemetry jumps fivefold for ten seconds. Gateway collectors scale on CPU, Kafka absorbs the burst, and the log ingesters work through their lag without slowing traces or metrics.

action.text: Every request sends telemetry to the node agents, then to gateway collectors behind a load balancer that hashes by trace ID.
A bad Checkout deploy logs every retry: five times the telemetry. The gateway collectors' CPU climbs and their HPA adds pods.
Kafka absorbs the logs. The ingesters fall behind for a while; traces and metrics, in their own topics, don't.
The deploy is rolled back and the ingesters catch up. Nothing was dropped.

simulations.title: Drill: Loki is down for ten seconds
simulations.description: Loki's write path fails. Kafka keeps every log for the ingesters while dashboards for traces and metrics carry on; when Loki returns, the backlog drains in order.

action.text: Logs, spans and metrics each have their own topic and consumers.
Drill: take down the Loki boundary. Kafka keeps the logs: nothing is lost, it just waits.
Loki is back and the ingesters drain the backlog. ClickHouse and the archive never stopped.
